concepts.name: Classification of committees and the composition of financial, business, scrutiny and department-related committees
concepts.description: Ad hoc and standing committees; strength, membership and chairmanship of the PAC, Estimates, COPU, business, DRSC and scrutiny committees.
concepts.idea: Each parliamentary committee has its own strength, House split and way of choosing the chairman, and the numbers differ by committee.
concepts.rule: Committees are ad hoc (inquiry and advisory, temporary) or standing. The Estimates Committee has 30 members, all from the Lok Sabha; the PAC and COPU have 22 each (15 LS + 7 RS), elected annually by STV, with the Speaker appointing the chairmen; by convention since 1967 the PAC chairman is from the Opposition. The Business Advisory Committee has 15 (LS) and 11 (RS) members and the Rules Committee 15 and 16; the Private Members committee and the Absence committee are Lok Sabha-only with 15 members. Each of the 24 DRSCs has 31 members (21 LS + 10 RS), nominated by the Speaker and the Chairman. Government Assurances and Papers Laid have 15 + 10; Subordinate Legislation 15 + 15; SC/ST Welfare and Women Empowerment 30 (20 + 10); Offices of Profit 15 (10 + 5).
concepts.example: A student must recall that the Estimates Committee is drawn only from the Lok Sabha whereas the PAC takes 7 members from the Rajya Sabha.

questions.q: Parliamentary committees are grouped into broad classes. Which one of the following committees belongs to the group of 'committees to scrutinise and control' rather than to the group of 'committees to inquire'?
questions.a: Joint Committee on Offices of Profit, with 15 members
o: Joint Committee on Offices of Profit, with 15 members
Committee on Petitions, with 15 members in the Lok Sabha
Committee of Privileges, with 15 members in the Lok Sabha
Ethics Committee, with 15 members in the Lok Sabha
questions.e: The scrutiny-and-control group lists Government Assurances, Papers Laid on the Table, Subordinate Legislation, Welfare of SCs and STs, Empowerment of Women and the Joint Committee on Offices of Profit (10 Lok Sabha and 5 Rajya Sabha members); Petitions, Privileges and Ethics form the 'inquire' group.
w: Committee on Petitions is a committee to inquire, not a scrutiny committee.
Committee of Privileges is a committee to inquire.
Ethics Committee is a committee to inquire.

questions.q: An Estimates Committee of 30 members is constituted every year. Which one of the following correctly describes how its membership is drawn?
questions.a: All 30 are elected by the Lok Sabha from among its own members by single transferable vote
o: All 30 are elected by the Lok Sabha from among its own members by single transferable vote
20 are elected by the Lok Sabha and 10 by the Rajya Sabha through proportional representation
15 are from the Lok Sabha and 7 from the Rajya Sabha, as in the Public Accounts Committee
All 30 are nominated by the Speaker from the Lok Sabha without any election
questions.e: The Estimates Committee has 30 members, all drawn from the Lok Sabha only, elected every year by the Lok Sabha by proportional representation through STV; the Speaker appoints its chairman from among them.
w: The Rajya Sabha has no representation on the Estimates Committee.
15+7 is the Public Accounts Committee and COPU pattern, which has 22 members.
Members are elected by the Lok Sabha through proportional representation (STV), not nominated.

questions.q: A new convention has been followed since 1967 regarding the chairman of a financial committee of Parliament. Which one of the following correctly states it?
questions.a: The Public Accounts Committee chairman is appointed by the Speaker and is drawn from the Opposition
o: The Public Accounts Committee chairman is appointed by the Speaker and is drawn from the Opposition
The Estimates Committee chairman is appointed by the Speaker and is drawn from the Opposition
The Public Accounts Committee chairman is elected by its members and is drawn from the ruling party
The Committee on Public Undertakings chairman is appointed by the Rajya Sabha Chairman from the Opposition
questions.e: By convention since 1967 the PAC chairman is chosen from the Opposition, and he is appointed by the Lok Sabha Speaker. The Estimates and COPU chairmen are appointed by the Speaker from Lok Sabha members.
w: The Estimates Committee chairman is generally from the ruling party.
The PAC chairman is appointed by the Speaker, not elected by the members, and the post goes to the Opposition.
The COPU chairman is appointed by the Speaker from among its Lok Sabha members.

questions.q: Among the committees relating to the day-to-day business of the House, one exists only in the Lok Sabha and has the Deputy Speaker as its chairman. Which one is it?
questions.a: Committee on Private Members' Bills and Resolutions
o: Committee on Private Members' Bills and Resolutions
Business Advisory Committee, which works in both Houses
Rules Committee, which works in both Houses of Parliament
Committee on Government Assurances, which works in both Houses
questions.e: The Private Members' committee has 15 members nominated by the Speaker, is a Lok Sabha body, and the Deputy Speaker is its chairman. In the Rajya Sabha, the Business Advisory Committee does that job.
w: The Business Advisory Committee works in both Houses and the presiding officer chairs it.
The Rules Committee works in both Houses with the presiding officer as chairman.
Government Assurances has separate committees in both Houses.

questions.q: As restructured in 2004, each Department-related Standing Committee has a fixed strength and a fixed Lok Sabha-Rajya Sabha ratio. Which one of the following is it?
questions.a: 31 members, 21 of them from the Lok Sabha
o: 31 members, 21 of them from the Lok Sabha
Forty-five members, 30 of them from the Lok Sabha
Thirty members, 20 of them from the Lok Sabha
Twenty-two members, 15 of them from the Lok Sabha
questions.e: There are 24 DRSCs, each with 31 members (21 LS and 10 RS), as restructured in July 2004.
w: 45 (30+15) was the earlier strength up to the 13th Lok Sabha, before the July 2004 restructuring.
30 (20+10) is the strength of the Committees on SC/ST Welfare and Empowerment of Women.
22 (15+7) is the strength of the PAC and COPU.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the classification of parliamentary committees:

1. Standing committees are temporary bodies constituted afresh whenever a particular issue arises.
2. Inquiry committees investigate specific matters of public importance; the Committee on Violation of Protocol Norms is an example.
3. A select committee on a Bill belongs to the inquiry class of ad hoc committees.
4. The two broad classes are ad hoc and standing committees, and ad hoc committees are temporary and cease to exist when their task is over.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: Standing committees are permanent in the sense that they are constituted periodically and work continuously; the temporary ones are ad hoc. Statement 2 is correct: Inquiry committees are a type of ad hoc committee; the protocol-norms committee is one of the examples listed. Statement 3 is incorrect: They are advisory committees, which consider and report on particular Bills. Statement 4 is correct: This is the basic classification of committees. Also.
w: '3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct:
'1 and 2 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct:

Consider the following statements about the composition of committees:

1. The Public Accounts Committee and the Committee on Public Undertakings each have 15 members from the Lok Sabha and 7 from the Rajya Sabha.
2. The Estimates Committee draws members from both Houses of Parliament.
3. The Rajya Sabha Business Advisory Committee has 11 members.

Consider the following statements about the chairmen of committees:

1. The chairman of the Estimates Committee is generally a member of the ruling party.
2. The chairman of the Committee on Public Undertakings is appointed by the Rajya Sabha Chairman from among the Rajya Sabha members.
3. The chairman of the Committee on Absence of Members from Sittings is appointed by the Speaker.

questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: The Speaker appoints him and he is generally from the ruling party; the Opposition convention belongs to the PAC. Statement 2 is incorrect: The Speaker appoints him from among its members; the Rajya Sabha Chairman has no such role. Statement 3 is correct: It is a Lok Sabha committee whose chairman the Speaker appoints. So 2 statement(s) are correct. Also.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: A Lok Sabha member who has been nominated to a Department-related Standing Committee ceases to be its member on being appointed a Minister.
Statement-II: The Lok Sabha members of a Department-related Standing Committee are nominated by the Speaker from among themselves.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct: a minister is not eligible for a DRSC and a member who becomes one ceases to be a member. Statement-II is correct: the Speaker nominates the Lok Sabha members and the Chairman the Rajya Sabha members. Who nominates the members is a separate matter from the ministerial disqualification, so II does not explain I.
w: Rejected: the nominating authority is not the reason a member leaves on becoming a Minister; the bar on Ministers is separate.
Rejected: Statement-II is correct, so the pair is not half-correct.
Rejected: Statement-I is correct: ceasing to be a member on appointment as a Minister is stated in the chapter.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: The presiding officer of a House is the ex-officio chairman of the Rules Committee of that House.
Statement-II: The Speaker is also the ex-officio chairman of the Committee on Private Members' Bills and Resolutions.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
o: Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct: the Speaker in the Lok Sabha and the Chairman in the Rajya Sabha are ex-officio chairmen of the Rules Committee. Statement-II is incorrect: the Deputy Speaker is the chairman of the Private Members' committee, which is a Lok Sabha body of 15 members.
w: Rejected: Statement-II is incorrect, so the pair cannot be both correct.
Rejected: Statement-II is incorrect, so there is nothing to explain or not explain.
Rejected: Statement-I is correct: the presiding officer of each House is ex-officio chairman of its Rules Committee.

Match each committee in List-I with the strength given in List-II
List-I
A. Committee on Subordinate Legislation
B. Committee on Offices of Profit
C. Committee on the Welfare of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes
D. A Departmentally Related Standing Committee

1. Thirty members, twenty of them from the Lok Sabha
2. Thirty-one members, twenty-one of them from the Lok Sabha

4. Fifteen members in each House
questions.e: A-4: Subordinate Legislation has 15 members in each House. B-3: Offices of Profit has 15 (10 LS + 5 RS). C-1: SC/ST Welfare has 30 (20+10). D-2: each DRSC has 31 (21+10).
w: A and B interchanged: 15 per House belongs to Subordinate Legislation; Offices of Profit is the 10+5 committee.
B and C interchanged: Offices of Profit is 10+5, SC/ST Welfare is 20+10.

concepts.name: Inquiry and house-keeping committees and the functions of the financial, DRSC, business and scrutiny committees
concepts.description: Strength of committees to inquire and house-keeping committees, and what the PAC, Estimates, COPU, DRSC, business and scrutiny committees do.
concepts.idea: A committee is identified by its function: the PAC audits spent money, the Estimates Committee suggests economy, COPU watches undertakings and DRSCs scrutinise demands beforehand.
concepts.rule: Petitions, Privileges and Ethics are committees to inquire (15 LS and 10 RS; the notes quote 13 for the Ethics RS committee, Laxmikanth gives 10). House-keeping committees: Library (9: 6 + 3), General Purposes, House and the Joint Committee on Salaries and Allowances (15: 10 + 5). The PAC examines appropriation accounts, finance accounts and CAG reports after spending (not demands for grants). The Estimates Committee, the continuous economy committee, suggests economies and the form of estimates and does not examine undertakings allotted to COPU. COPU examines undertakings run on sound business principles. DRSCs cover all ministries (8 under the RS, 16 under the LS). Scrutiny committees check assurances, delegated legislation, papers laid, SC/ST and women welfare, and offices of profit.
concepts.example: A bill on delegated rules goes to the Subordinate Legislation Committee while a statutory notification is not examined by the Papers Laid committee.

questions.q: Four committees of Parliament are listed below. Which one has 15 members in the Lok Sabha and 15 members in the Rajya Sabha, as separate committees?
o: Committee on Papers Laid on the Table
questions.e: Subordinate Legislation is 15 + 15; the other three scrutiny and inquiry committees named are 15 + 10.
w: Government Assurances has 15 in the Lok Sabha and 10 in the Rajya Sabha.
Papers Laid on the Table has 15 in the Lok Sabha and 10 in the Rajya Sabha.
Petitions has 15 in the Lok Sabha and 10 in the Rajya Sabha.

questions.q: Which one of the following is a house-keeping (service) committee, that is, one concerned with facilities and services for members?
questions.a: Joint Committee on Salaries and Allowances of Members
o: Joint Committee on Salaries and Allowances of Members
Joint Committee on Offices of Profit, which examines bodies set up by governments
Committee on Petitions, which examines petitions on Bills
Rules Committee, which recommends changes in the Rules of Procedure
questions.e: House-keeping committees include the Library Committee, General Purposes Committee, House Committee and the Joint Committee on Salaries and Allowances.
w: Offices of Profit is a scrutiny committee.
Petitions is a committee to inquire.
Rules is a day-to-day business committee.

questions.q: The Library Committee of Parliament is a joint committee. Which one of the following gives its composition?
questions.a: Nine members, the Rajya Sabha supplying three of them
o: Nine members, the Rajya Sabha supplying three of them
Fifteen members, the Rajya Sabha supplying five of them
Twelve members, the Rajya Sabha supplying four of them
Nine members, the Rajya Sabha supplying six of them
questions.e: The Library Committee has 9 members, 6 from the Lok Sabha and 3 from the Rajya Sabha.
w: 15 (10+5) is the Joint Committee on Salaries and Allowances.
The Library Committee is not 12; the House Committee has 12 members in the Lok Sabha.

questions.q: A student is asked what the Public Accounts Committee actually scrutinises. Which one of the following is correct?
questions.a: The appropriation and finance accounts, with the CAG's audit reports
o: The appropriation and finance accounts, with the CAG's audit reports
The demands for grants of the ministries, before the Lok Sabha votes on them
The budget estimates, so as to suggest economies in public spending year after year
The working of public undertakings against sound business principles and commercial practice
questions.e: The PAC examines the appropriation and finance accounts and the CAG's audit reports, that is, spending after the event. A claim that it examines demands for grants before voting is wrong; the DRSCs consider demands before voting.
w: Demands for grants are examined beforehand by the Department-related Standing Committees; the PAC works after the money is spent.
That is the function of the Estimates Committee.
That is the function of the Committee on Public Undertakings.

questions.q: A parliamentary committee may examine the estimates throughout the financial year and report to the Lok Sabha as its examination proceeds; it need not examine the entire estimates of any one year. This describes the
questions.e: The Estimates Committee, called the continuous economy committee, may examine estimates from time to time through the year and report as it proceeds.
w: The PAC examines accounts and audit reports after expenditure.
COPU examines public undertakings' reports and accounts.
Government Assurances examines ministers' promises.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Public Accounts Committee:

1. It examines the demands for grants of ministries before they are voted by the Lok Sabha.
2. It brings to Parliament's notice cases of extravagance, wasteful or unfruitful expenditure and lack of financial integrity.
3. Under Article 151, the CAG's reports are submitted to the President, laid before Parliament, and then examined by the committee.
4. It satisfies itself that expenditure was authorised by Parliament and that spending under each head did not exceed the authorisation.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: That is done by the Department-related Standing Committees; the PAC examines accounts after the spending. Statement 2 is correct: These are its core concerns. Statement 3 is correct: Art. 151 provides for audit reports to be laid before Parliament. Statement 4 is correct: This is the check made on appropriation accounts. Also.
w: '1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct:
'2 and 4 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct:
'1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct:

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Estimates Committee:

1. It reports on the economies and administrative reform consistent with the policy underlying the estimates, and suggests alternative policies for efficiency.
2. It advises on the format in which the budget estimates ought to be placed before Parliament.
3. It is bound to examine the entire estimates of a financial year before the demands for grants can be voted.
4. It examines the public sector undertakings along with the Committee on Public Undertakings.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: First and second listed functions. Statement 2 is correct: A listed function. Statement 3 is incorrect: It is not incumbent on it to examine all estimates, and the demands may be voted even if it has made no report. Statement 4 is incorrect: Undertakings allotted to COPU are outside its functions. Also.
w: '1 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct:
'2 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct:
'1 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct:

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Committee on Public Undertakings (COPU):

1. It examines the reports and accounts of public undertakings to ensure financial prudence.
2. It examines whether the affairs of the undertakings are managed in accordance with sound business principles and prudent commercial practices.
3. It examines the reports of the Comptroller and Auditor-General on the public undertakings.
4. It also examines matters of major government policy relating to the undertakings.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: examining the reports and accounts of public undertakings is the committee's first function. Statement 2 is correct: testing whether the undertakings are run on sound business principles and prudent commercial practices is another of its functions. Statement 3 is correct: examining the CAG's reports on the public undertakings is one of its functions. Statement 4 is incorrect: matters of major government policy are expressly outside its scope, as are day-to-day administration matters. So 1, 2 and 3 only.
w: '1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect (major policy is outside its scope), and leaves out statement 3, which is correct.
'1, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect (major policy is outside its scope), and leaves out statement 2, which is correct.
'1, 2, 3 and 4' includes statement 4, which is incorrect (major policy is outside its scope).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Department-related Standing Committees (DRSCs):

1. Of the 24 DRSCs, 16 work under the Rajya Sabha and 8 under the Lok Sabha.
2. The 24 committees together cover all the ministries and departments of the Central Government.

concepts.name: Consultative committees, JPCs, Ethics and Privileges committees and Parliamentary Forums
concepts.description: Consultative committees; JPCs; the Ethics committees of the two Houses; the Privileges Committee and breach of privilege procedure; Parliamentary Forums.
concepts.idea: Consultative committees are informal and not parliamentary committees, while Ethics and Privileges committees inquire into conduct and privilege breaches and recommend, but the House decides.
concepts.rule: Consultative committees are constituted by the Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs with 10-30 members, chaired by the minister, and are not parliamentary committees. JPCs have members of both Houses and may take evidence. The Rajya Sabha Ethics Committee was established on 4 March 1997 by Chairman K. R. Narayanan; the Lok Sabha had an ad hoc one from 2000 (Speaker Balayogi) and a permanent one from 2015. The Privileges Committee is semi-judicial and recommends action; breach of privilege may be of the House or of a member; any member can raise a question, the presiding officer refers it on a prima facie case, and the House acts on the committee report. Parliamentary Forums are informal platforms with the Speaker as ex-officio President.
concepts.example: A newspaper imputing corruption to a member is a breach of the member privilege, referred only after the Speaker finds a prima facie case.

questions.q: Consultative committees attached to ministries are constituted by one Ministry, and their membership is bounded by a minimum and a maximum. Which one of the following is correct?
questions.a: Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs; between 10 and 30 members
o: Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs; between 10 and 30 members
Ministry of Law and Justice, which also frames their guidelines; between 10 and 30 members
Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs; between 15 and 45 members, the old DRSC strength
Lok Sabha Secretariat, acting under the Speaker; between 5 and 25 members
questions.e: Consultative committees are constituted by the Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs, which also frames the guidelines; membership runs from 10 to 30.
w: The constituting Ministry is Parliamentary Affairs, not Law and Justice.
The range is 10 to 30; 15 and 45 mix up with the old DRSC strength.
The Lok Sabha Secretariat does not constitute them.

questions.q: Consultative committees, though made up of Members of Parliament, are not parliamentary committees. Which one of the following is the reason?
questions.a: They fail the four tests of a parliamentary committee, such as having a House secretariat
o: They fail the four tests of a parliamentary committee, such as having a House secretariat
They are appointed by the Prime Minister, whereas a parliamentary committee must be elected by the House itself
They are drawn from the Rajya Sabha, whereas a parliamentary committee must have members from both Houses
They are standing bodies that Parliament constitutes afresh each year, unlike the ad hoc committees of the Houses
questions.e: A parliamentary committee is appointed or elected by the House or nominated by the presiding officer, works under his direction, reports to the House or to him, and has a secretariat provided by the Lok Sabha or Rajya Sabha. Consultative committees are constituted by the Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs and do not fulfil these tests, so they are not parliamentary committees.
w: They are constituted by the Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs, not appointed by the Prime Minister; and a parliamentary committee may also be nominated by the Speaker or Chairman.
They consist of members of both Houses of Parliament.
They are reconstituted with each Lok Sabha, not each year, and standing committees are parliamentary committees too.

w: Chatterjee became Speaker only in 2004.

Sangma's term as Speaker ended in 1998.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements about breach of privilege and contempt of the House is correct?
questions.a: Every breach of privilege amounts to contempt of the House, though some contempts breach no specific privilege
o: Every breach of privilege amounts to contempt of the House, though some contempts breach no specific privilege
Every contempt of the House is a breach of privilege, though some breaches of privilege are not contempts
A single statute passed by Parliament now lists all privileges, so the unwritten sources no longer apply
The two expressions are identical in meaning, and Article 105 defines both of them in full for each House
questions.e: A breach of privilege is a clear violation of a specific privilege and is always a contempt; contempt is the wider concept, covering offences against the dignity and authority of the House, e.g. disobedience to a legitimate order of the House. Parliament has not exhaustively codified privileges, which rest on five sources.
w: The relation is the reverse: contempt is the wider idea.
Parliament has not yet made a special law to codify all privileges.
The chapter distinguishes the two; Article 105 expressly mentions only freedom of speech and the right of publication.

questions.q: A member alleges that a newspaper has committed a breach of privilege. At which point does the Privileges Committee come into the procedure?
questions.a: After the presiding officer finds a prima facie case and refers the matter
o: After the presiding officer finds a prima facie case and refers the matter
As soon as any member raises the question, before the presiding officer has formed any view on it
After the House has voted on and adopted a motion of censure against the newspaper's editor
After the President, on the advice of the Council of Ministers, directs that it be referred
questions.e: Any member may raise a question of privilege; if the Speaker or Chairman finds a prima facie case, it is referred to the Privileges Committee, which inquires and reports to the House.
w: A reference needs the presiding officer's satisfaction of a prima facie case.
No censure motion is the first step.
The President plays no role in the procedure.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about consultative committees:

1. They are constituted to promote regular interaction and consultation between Members of Parliament and the Government.
2. The Minister or Minister of State in charge of the ministry concerned acts as chairman of its consultative committee.
3. The Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs frames the guidelines on their composition, functions and procedure.
4. They continue to function through the dissolution of the Lok Sabha and are not reconstituted after a general election.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: they exist to promote regular interaction and consultation between Members of Parliament and the Government. Statement 2 is correct: the Minister or Minister of State in charge of the ministry concerned is the chairman of its committee. Statement 3 is correct: the Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs frames the guidelines on composition, functions and procedure and also arranges the meetings. Statement 4 is incorrect: they stand dissolved on every dissolution of the Lok Sabha and are reconstituted for each new Lok Sabha. So 1, 2 and 3 only.
w: '2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect (they are reconstituted after each general election), and leaves out statement 1, which is correct
'2 and 3 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct (they exist to promote interaction between members and the Government)
'1, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect (they are reconstituted after each general election), and leaves out statement 2, which is correct

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

w: '2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct
'1, 2, 3 and 4' includes statement 3, which is incorrect

Statement 4 is correct: the Committee on Installation of Portraits and Statues of National Leaders and Parliamentarians in the Parliament House Complex is likewise an ad hoc committee. So all four are correct.
w: '1, 2 and 4 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct (the Library Committee is a standing house-keeping committee)

3. The Ethics Committee is classed among the committees to scrutinise and control rather than those to inquire.

Statement 2 is correct: it examines cases of misconduct referred to it and recommends appropriate action to the House. Statement 3 is incorrect: the Ethics Committee, with the Committees on Petitions and Privileges, is classed among the committees to inquire, not those to scrutinise and control. Statement 4 is correct: the Rajya Sabha committee has 10 members against 15 in the Lok Sabha. So 2 and 4 only.
w: '1 and 2 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect (the Houses have separate Ethics Committees), and leaves out statement 4, which is correct
'3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect (it is a committee to inquire), and leaves out statement 2, which is correct
'4 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct (it examines misconduct cases and recommends action)

Statement 3 is correct: it inquires and reports to the House, which then acts on the report. So 1 and 3 only.

2. Parliamentary privileges are based on a single codified statute enacted by Parliament.

questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: privileges are enjoyed collectively by each House and individually by members. Statement 2 is incorrect: They rest on five sources: constitutional provisions, laws, rules of the Houses, conventions and judicial interpretations; Parliament has not codified them. Statement 3 is correct: This is the definition of contempt. Statement 4 is incorrect: It is the standard example of contempt that is not a breach of a specific privilege.

2. Consultative committees exercise formal scrutiny and oversight over the executive in the way parliamentary committees do.

So 2 statement(s) are correct.

concepts.name: Indian Parliamentary Group, IPU and CPA, committee comparison and emergency provisions overview
concepts.description: Origin, membership, office-bearers and functions of the IPG; IPU and CPA links; the financial committee comparison; the Part XVIII emergency articles.
concepts.idea: The IPG is an autonomous body of MPs that is the National Group of the IPU and the India branch of the CPA.
concepts.rule: The IPG was formed in 1949 on a motion of the Constituent Assembly (Legislative) of 16 August 1948. All sitting MPs can be members; former MPs are associate members without representation at IPU/CPA meetings or travel concessions. The Speaker is ex-officio President, the Deputy Speaker and the RS Deputy Chairman are Vice-Presidents, and the Lok Sabha Secretary-General is its Secretary-General. It arranges delegations, addresses, seminars and letters of introduction; only members of six months standing can join delegations abroad. The PAC and COPU share the 15 + 7 pattern, only the Estimates Committee is wholly from the Lok Sabha. Emergency provisions are in Part XVIII (Articles 352-360): Art. 352, Art. 356, Art. 360.
concepts.example: An MP who joined the IPG two months ago cannot be put on a delegation abroad.
